Newcastle's 'angry and frustrated' fans to stage a mass walkout in the second half of Cardiff visit

Newcastle United fans are planning to stage a mass walkout during this weekend's Cardiff City game in protest of the way the club is being run.

A statement from the Newcastle United Supporters' Trust have claimed that supporters are "angry and frustrated" about the state of the affairs at the club.

The Magpies have lost their last six games, shipping 17 goals and scoring just two in that time.

Many fans are calling for manager Alan Pardew to be sacked, while club owner Mike Ashley has often been a controversial figure at St James' Park.

The NUST release read: "As fans we have deep concerns at the direction Newcastle United is heading in, both on and off the pitch.

"The vast majority of supporters are angry and frustrated but are divided as to what, if anything, can be done to positively influence Mike Ashley and those who run the football club on his behalf."

Their frustrations are set to culminate in a mass exit midway through the second half against the Welsh club.

The 69th minute has been chosen, due to its significance of when the club last won a trophy - the 1969 Inter City Fairs Cup.

Newcastle United fans' group protest against Alan Pardew by printing banners parodying Mike Ashley

Newcastle United fans' group step up protest against Alan Pardew by printing thousands of banners parodying owner Mike Ashley's Sports Direct company 

08:50 EDT 18 Sep 2014, updated 12:27 EDT 18 Sep 2014

 * Section of Newcastle United fans have created 'SackPardew.com' website
 * The campaign aims to force the removal of Magpies boss Alan Pardew
 * More than 200 banners and 15,000 posters have been printed by group 
 * Campaign logo is a parody on owner Mike Ashley's Sports Direct symbol
 * Aim is for banners to be displayed during Newcastle's match with Hull City
 * Group have contacted club ahead of Saturday's St James' Park clash
 * Newcastle were hammered 4-0 at St Mary's by Southampton last weekend
 * Magpies sit bottom of the Premier League with two points from four games 
 * See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The determination from a section of Newcastle United fans to remove Alan Pardew from his position as manager has ramped up another notch as thousands of posters were printed demanding the 53-year-old be sacked.

A campaign named SackPardew.com has grown immeasurably in its endeavours to convince owner Mike Ashley to dispense with the Magpies boss as frustration mounts on Tyneside.

And the group behind the website claim they have printed more than 200 banners and 15,000 posters ready to be displayed when the Premier League's basement-boys host Hull City on Saturday - with the text used a parody on the Sports Direct logo, the company which Ashley owns.

The group contacted The Chronicle and told the paper they were confident the banners could be taken into St James' Park without any hassle.

They said: 'They (the banners) are small enough to conceal so we can get them into the stadium, but we don't want to go down that road.

'We have contacted the club to let them know our plans and are still waiting to hear back from them.

'We have also let the police and council know our plans. We want this to be peaceful and well organised.' 

Having contracted the support of many pubs in Newcastle, fans will be able to collect banners from specific locations which will be revealed by the group before the match.

VIDEO Pardew on the edge  

A protest van emblazoned with the campaign's logo will also drive to some of Newcastle's most-recognisable landmarks ahead of the game.


Large banners were already held aloft emblazoned with the name of the website and with a smiling picture of Pardew during Newcastle's embarrassing 4-0 hammering at St Mary's last weekend. 

There were also fans' posters with the messages 'Pardew out' and 'Pardew is a muppet' displayed in the away end on the south coast. 

It seems that the defeat at Southampton prompted an acceleration of the campaign as photos show boxes and boxes of signs bearing the slogan being printed across the city.

The Magpies are yet to win a game this season and sit bottom of the Premier League with just two points from four matches.

webpage.text:
Newcastle assistant manager John Carver apologises for confronting fans | Newcastle United

Newcastle United’s assistant manager John Carver has apologised to fans after swearing at a section of the travelling support at St Mary’s Stadium.

During the 4-0 defeat by Southampton on Saturday, the visitors’ manager Alan Pardew was subjected to abuse by Newcastle fans who sang “You’re getting sacked in the morning” and chanted the name of Hatem Ben Arfa, who Pardew sent on loan to Hull City.

At the end of the game a fan had to be wrestled to the grass by stewards before he could confront Pardew, who declined to speak to the press afterwards, a total of seven local and national newspapers having been banned by the club.

During the game Carver was seen pointing to and apparently swearing at a section of the travelling support who were holding a “Pardew Out” banner.

His actions resulted in complaints from the fans and, in a statement published on Newcastle’s website on Thursday, Carver insisted he was sorry, saying: “I sincerely apologise for any offence caused by my reaction.”

The full statement said: “Newcastle United received a number of complaints from supporters regarding the conduct of its coaching staff during and after the defeat to Southampton on Saturday, 13th September. This matter has now been dealt with internally.

“Following the conclusion of the club’s inquiries, assistant manager John Carver, said: ‘My sole focus on Saturday, as it always is, was on trying to gain three points for Newcastle United and preparing the players to the best of my ability.

‘This included keeping them focused on their roles and duties in the upcoming 90 minutes.

‘In the warm-up, I was disappointed to see banners that could, in my opinion, distract the players and take focus away from the job in hand – namely winning the match.

‘I went over to our fans to ask them to help us and requested that they take the banners down. The vast majority of supporters back the team through thick and thin and I am very proud to be one of them.

‘I was met with abuse from one supporter and I regret that I responded inappropriately. I sincerely apologise for any offence caused by my reaction.

‘Every fan is entitled to an opinion, positive or negative, and I respect that. I hope fans will understand that I, like them, only wanted what was best for the team.

‘I am proud to work for my home town club and would ask every supporter to back the players and all staff, as they really can make a difference.’”

Meanwhile the goalkeeping coach Andy Woodman apologised for what he described as “the ill-advised comment I posted privately on Twitter on Sunday morning, which was subsequently made public.

“It was never my intention, of course, for my response to enter the public domain. My response was a reaction to significant personal abuse I received from a number of fans which I felt exceeded that which was fair and balanced.

“That said, I understand my response was unacceptable and I regret my actions and apologise for any offence caused.”

The Twitter account appears to have since been taken down.

Newcastle face Hull at St James’ Park on Saturday with the Tigers’ manager Steve Bruce among those tipped to replace Pardew should the owner Mike Ashley decide a change of direction is needed in the dugout.

webpage.text:
Alan Pardew: Should Newcastle United back or sack their under-pressure manager?

Our man in the North East, Simon Bird, looks at the pros and cons of dispensing with the Premier League's second-longest-serving manager


Alan Pardew insists he has a "long term" future at Newcastle, despite a fans revolt.

The United boss is battling a run of terrible form, including six defeats in a row, which has seen Geordies turn against him, with some fans demanding his head.

But Pardew is planning summer transfers, and has already arranged two pre-season training trips as he looks ahead to next season.

The head coach will face talks with owner Mike Ashley at the end of the season. Last year he came close to being sacked after a poor campaign when relegation was narrowly avoided.

Ashley has to decide whether to back his boss, or sack him amid growing unrest.

However he is also ready to pay out a multi-million pound bonus pot to players and all club staff if Newcastle clinch a top ten finish against Cardiff this weekend.

Pardew said: "I'm looking at the job as a long-term opportunity for myself. That's how you have to focus.

"I know they're disappointed and angry at the moment that we haven't got a result."

That leaves Ashley with a decision to make.

Here are my five reasons to sack or back Pardew:


Sack.....


RESULTS : Pardew claimed last week that Newcastle were battling against a "short term" run of bad results which now extends to a club record six defeats in a row in the Premier League.

Actually it is a longer term problem problem dating back to early January. Newcastle have lost 14 out of their last 19 games.

If that had happened at the start of the season they would be deep in relegation trouble. If the form/defeats continue early next season there will be a mid-season crisis to deal with. Is it better to change manager now, than after five games of next season?

GOALS : The statistics are damning, and prove Newcastle have an over reliance in Loic Remywho they don't even own, and the sold Yohan Cabaye.

They have managed one goal in their last six games. They have failed to score in 13 of their last 18 games.

Worst of all they have netted only ten times in the league in 2014, the worst record in the division.

ATTITUDE : Recent performances have been blighted by a set of players who look to have given up for the season weeks ago, once relegation looked unlikely. Some are protecting themselves before the World Cup.

Has Pardew's authority evaporated since his headbutt disgrace at Hull, and subsequent stadium and touchline ban? Players left some boxing gloves in his office as a joke, but Pardew concedes some were probably happy to see him being hammered for his actions.

It all adds up to a lethargic team who have lacked fight, passion and prone to sloppy personal errors that have cost goals.

It's Pardew's main job to get the best out of the players he has got, and he's failed to do that. And then there is the sidelining of Hatem Ben Arfa, potentially the most creative, danger on the books.

FAN PROTESTS : Discontent has been brewing for weeks, but is not being shown on the terraces. It is hard to determine what percentage of fans want Pardew sacked, but the feelings of the travelling away fans are clear. They mocked Pardew with chants at Arsenal and banners saying: Pardew out.

Once there is a toxic feeling to a manager's reign there is often no way back. Pardew has certainly run out of credit and credibility, with a significant number of fans.

EXCUSES : Pardew is being undermined by his usually slick pre and post match chat. Every word he says is seen as an excuse, and passing the blame.

Injuries, officials, pressure, Europe, unrealistic expectations. Fans are weary that with every defeat comes a fresh reason why it has gone wrong.

It seems at times that Pardew can't say anything that doesn't inflame the situation.


Five reasons for Pardew to stay.....


TARGET ACHIEVED : A top ten finish was the target set by owner Mike Ashley, and Pardew and his players have delivered. The current position of ninth is about par for the course at Newcastle in terms of budgets of their rivals.

A bonus will be paid out to players and all club staff. It is hard to sack a manager who has just collected a bonus for meeting a target.

BEST PLAYER SOLD : The £16m sale of Yohan Cabaye in January was a devastating blow on and off the pitch. The creative force was gone. The man who opened up defences and set the tone in the dressing room sold.

No only did it rob United of guile, it left players, especially the French contingent, deflated. It was not just the fans who were let questioning the ambition of the club.

Every Newcastle manager, not just Pardew, will have to be prepared to sell their best player for top value. That is a club policy, and a problem only owner Mike Ashley can change.

BOTTOM OF SPENDING LEAGUE : In the last five years, Newcastle have made a pds 45 million profit in the transfer market according to some estimates.

By the time the summer window opens it will be 18 months since they've landed a permanent new signing. Squads go stale when not refreshed and added to.

Pardew was left high and dry by the failure to replace Cabaye in January, but says he has a war chest to rebuild in the summer. That will go a long way to relaunching his reign.


MIKE ASHLEY : The owner has created a club with strong finances, which makes a profit, and runs itself. The main aim seems to be stay in the top flight. However fans believe the cup competitions should be priority too, something that the hierarchy doesn't seem to appreciate.

There will always be a ceiling to Newcastle's potential when they are shopping for bargains abroad. Pardew and fans argue that with 52k crowds, and a top half team, there should also be scope for United to sign a top player for £10-12 million and not set fees at half that amount.

STABILITY : Given the constraints at Newcastle who would do a better job? Which manager within Newcastle's reach would accept all the limitations Pardew does, and get them top half, and two years ago, into fifth?

Every manager has a shelf life, but Newcastle have gone down the regular sackings route for years, and still own nothing. Why not just back Pardew to rebuild - after all his tactical plan got Newcastle up to fifth place again at the end of November.

webpage.text:
Does Alan Pardew even realise he has turned Newcastle United into a laughing stock? | Football

| Work in communications. MCIPR + Accredited. Former daily news journalist. Dog owner. Classic car enthusiast. Beatles fan. NUFC supporter. All views are my own.

Published April 20, 2014 8:45pm Updated December 10, 2019 9:40am

Alan Pardew became the first Newcastle United manager in the Premier League era to lose five consecutive games – then performed his own Easter miracle by holding on to his job.

The former manager of the year has also overseen the Toon’s heaviest top-flight defeat, and is the first Magpies manager for decades to lead the side to three consecutive derby defeats.

Worst still, if the Toon fail to score two more goals at St James’ Park against Cardiff – who ended the Magpie’s FA Cup run before it had started – Pardew will be able to add Newcastle’s worst home goals return in a top-flight season to his list of failures.

Newcastle must have the hardest working team in the league after Pardew again claimed his defeated players will be increasing their efforts in training.

Despite talk of Crystal Palace’s messiah Tony Pulis being targeted to take charge by owner Mike Ashley, and regardless of how many opportunities the manager hands him on a plate to cancel his long-term contract, it’s clear that the Sports Direct tycoon has no intention of ending his current manager’s stay on Tyneside.

Yet it is clear Pardew is running out of ideas and excuses.

His starting line-up as the Magpie’s took to the field against Swansea City stank of tactical desperation.

Former Dutch international, and holding midfielder, Vurnon Anita was at right-back; the club’s number nine and centre-forward Papiss Cisse was picked at right midfield and forward thinking Yoan Gouffran was playing on left midfield.

His centre-forward pairing of Shola Ameobi and Luuke De Jong– prior to kick-off – shared a goal-drought lasting well over two years.

The decision to leave star-striker Loic Remy and fellow French international Mathieu Debuchy on the bench suggested arrogant Pardew was underestimating the Welsh side even before a ball was kicked.

Before the 4-0 defeat at Southampton, which signalled Pardew’s return to football stadia after his ban, the manager boldly claimed his return would ‘revive the dressing room’ and install a ‘winning mentality’.

He was up to his old tricks again on Saturday insisting that, if he was on the touchline, he could have influenced the situation which led to one time Toon target Wilfried Bony’s match-winning penalty.

The Toon still have to travel to Arsenal and Liverpool, meaning the visit of struggling Cardiff City is the Magpie’s only realistic chance of earning three points between now and the end of the season.

In the days before the disappointing home encounter captain Fabrico Coloccini claimed the players had ‘achieved our goal of finishing in the top 10’, allegedly earning the squad a bonus, but after the Easter weekend’s results 11th placed Crystal Palace are just three points behind the Magpies and the resurgent Eagles already have a better goal difference.

Don’t spend it yet skip.

Alan Pardew became the first Newcastle United manager in the Premier League era to lose five consecutive games – then performed his own Easter miracle by holding on to his job.The former manager of the year has also overseen the Toon’s heaviest top-flight defeat, and is the first Magpies manager for decades to lead the side to three consecutive derby defeats.Worst still, if the Toon fail to score two more goals at St James’ Park against Cardiff – who ended the Magpie’s FA Cup run before it had started – Pardew will be able to add Newcastle’s worst home goals return in a top-flight season to his list of failures.Newcastle must have the hardest working team in the league after Pardew again claimed his defeated players will be increasing their efforts in training.Despite talk of Crystal Palace’s messiah Tony Pulis being targeted to take charge by owner Mike Ashley, and regardless of how many opportunities the manager hands him on a plate to cancel his long-term contract, it’s clear that the Sports Direct tycoon has no intention of ending his current manager’s stay on Tyneside.Yet it is clear Pardew is running out of ideas and excuses.His starting line-up as the Magpie’s took to the field against Swansea City stank of tactical desperation.Former Dutch international, and holding midfielder, Vurnon Anita was at right-back; the club’s number nine and centre-forward Papiss Cisse was picked at right midfield and forward thinking Yoan Gouffran was playing on left midfield.His centre-forward pairing of Shola Ameobi and Luuke De Jong– prior to kick-off – shared a goal-drought lasting well over two years.

The decision to leave star-striker Loic Remy and fellow French international Mathieu Debuchy on the bench suggested arrogant Pardew was underestimating the Welsh side even before a ball was kicked.Before the 4-0 defeat at Southampton, which signalled Pardew’s return to football stadia after his ban, the manager boldly claimed his return would ‘revive the dressing room’ and install a ‘winning mentality’.He was up to his old tricks again on Saturday insisting that, if he was on the touchline, he could have influenced the situation which led to one time Toon target Wilfried Bony’s match-winning penalty.The Toon still have to travel to Arsenal and Liverpool, meaning the visit of struggling Cardiff City is the Magpie’s only realistic chance of earning three points between now and the end of the season.In the days before the disappointing home encounter captain Fabrico Coloccini claimed the players had ‘achieved our goal of finishing in the top 10’, allegedly earning the squad a bonus, but after the Easter weekend’s results 11th placed Crystal Palace are just three points behind the Magpies and the resurgent Eagles already have a better goal difference.Don’t spend it yet skip.

jsonld.headline: Does Alan Pardew even realise he has turned Newcastle United into a laughing stock?

resultats_lens.texte_contexte: Alan Pardew faces continued scrutiny as Newcastle United manager after a poor run of form, heavy defeats, and tactical choices, despite owner Mike Ashley retaining him, while players and management prepare for upcoming matches against Swansea City and Cardiff City.
